findings.title: Queues are unbounded, so the consumer has no backpressure
findings.body: Each worker queue is created as an unbounded `queue.Queue()`, while `submit` immediately returns after enqueueing. A slow group/worker can therefore accumulate every subsequently polled Kafka message in memory; increasing the configured worker count only changes the number of unbounded queues. Under sustained input or a stuck downstream dependency this can exhaust process memory rather than applying backpressure to Kafka, contrary to the strategy's stated behavior.

findings.title: Worker exceptions are acknowledged as successfully processed
findings.body: The worker catches every exception from `result_processor` and then unconditionally calls `complete_offset` in `finally`. The commit loop can consequently commit the failed message and all later contiguous messages, permanently dropping a result after a transient database, network, or application failure. This also contradicts the strategy's documented guarantee that offsets are committed only after successful processing; failures need to remain outstanding or be handled through an explicit retry/DLQ policy.

findings.title: Graceful shutdown stops workers before queued work is drained
findings.body: `shutdown` sets every worker's `shutdown` flag before attempting to shut down the queue. A worker finishes at most the item it is currently processing and then exits its `while not self.shutdown` loop, leaving all remaining queued items unprocessed. Normal consumer shutdown/rebalance therefore abandons queued work rather than draining it, causing replayed side effects on restart and preventing a graceful shutdown from completing its in-flight workload.

findings.title: Shutdown relies on Python 3.13-only queue APIs
findings.body: `Queue.shutdown()` and `queue.ShutDown` were introduced in Python 3.13. On Python 3.12 and earlier, `q.shutdown(...)` raises `AttributeError` (which is only logged), blocked worker threads remain stuck in `get()`, and the configured joins time out. The implementation must use a compatible sentinel/wakeup mechanism or raise the project's minimum Python version before using these APIs.
